# E0 minimal public fixture

This directory contains synthetic, bilingual LaTeX/Word review content. It is
designed for repeatable upstream contract tests and contains no private paper,
unpublished result, real reviewer, or personal metadata. The paper, review
text, identities, timestamps, figure and bibliography are original synthetic
material; the DOCX package is seeded from the MIT-licensed `python-docx` 1.2.0
default template.

## Contents

- `source/`: a multi-file LaTeX article with English and Chinese text, inline
  and display mathematics, labels/references, one figure, one table, and a
  synthetic bibliography entry.
- `base/review-base.docx`: a clean review document generated from the same
  synthetic subject matter.
- `returned/returned-reviewed.docx`: a derivative of the base DOCX containing
  real OOXML insertions, deletions, a replacement, a move pair, a run-format
  revision, and point/range comments.
- `expected-structure.json`: manually specified structural counts.
- `expected-changeset.json`: the independent oracle for review events. It is
  not generated by any candidate parser under test.
- `provenance.json`: origin, redistribution status, generator versions, and
  SHA-256 values.

The reviewer names `Reviewer Alpha` and `Reviewer Beta` and all timestamps are
fixed synthetic test data. They must remain visible in the returned DOCX so
revision readers can be tested; they are not personal metadata.

Original fixture content is licensed under the repository's Apache-2.0
license. Redistributed DOCX template members retain the python-docx MIT notice
in `third_party/python-docx-LICENSE.txt`; full component scope is recorded in
`provenance.json`. Regenerate the binary files from a clean clone using the
repository-declared fixture dependencies; no Codex skill or private helper is
required:

```powershell
uv sync --locked --group fixture
uv run --locked --group fixture python scripts/build_e0_public_fixture.py
```

The generated ZIP metadata, authors, and review timestamps are fixed. The
generator writes a machine-readable summary to `build/e0-cleanroom/` so two
independent rebuilds can be compared before committing refreshed binaries.
